change.describe: branch `pr-67876-flat` of sentry-67876-flat against f3b740199ef0b8057c2c68a377fd3b4d42346deb (merge-base f3b7401)
change.title: pr-67876-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: OAuth `state` is a constant, so it gives no CSRF protection
findings.body: `state = pipeline.signature`, and `signature` is `md5_text(*pipe_ids)` over the view class names (src/sentry/pipeline/base.py:132-133). Every user and every session gets the same value; the tests hardcode `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`. The check at line 412 therefore can't tell a callback this session started from a forged one. An attacker can send someone who is mid-pipeline to `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker's code>&state=9cae…`. That binds `github_authenticated_user` to the attacker's GitHub login (login CSRF), and the new sender check exists to protect exactly that value. Fix: generate a random per-pipeline nonce, `bind_state` it before the redirect, and compare it with `constant_time_compare` on return.

findings.title: `metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError for integrations created through the Sentry pipeline
findings.body: `build_integration` only writes `metadata["sender"]` when the state has a sender (lines 376-377). The webhook passes one (webhook.py:204-207), but the pipeline state doesn't, and `test_basic_flow` confirms metadata without `sender` (test_integration.py:303-310). Deleting an OrganizationIntegration does not delete the Integration (deletions/defaults/organizationintegration.py). So a user who installed through Sentry, uninstalled, and then reinstalls (into the same or another org) reaches this line with an existing Integration, no OrganizationIntegration and no `sender`. The result is an unhandled KeyError (500) instead of an error page. `installation.py:44` already guards this with `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`. Handle the missing key explicitly: render `error(...)`, or decide what should be allowed.

findings.title: Network failures or GitHub errors in the OAuth exchange give a 500, not the error dialog
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` runs outside the `try`, so a connection error or timeout escapes. `get_user_info` (identity/github/provider.py:7-17) calls `resp.raise_for_status()` and `resp.json()` with no handling, so a 401 from `/user` (expired or revoked token) or a non-JSON body also escapes. Every other failure in this view renders `github-integration-failed.html`, which posts `success: false` to the opener window. These paths instead leave the popup on a 500 page and the opener never gets a message. Put both calls inside the `try` and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

findings.title: The installer check is skipped whenever the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: The new sender comparison only runs when an Integration already exists. If the `installation` webhook hasn't arrived yet (or failed), the code goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()`. `build_integration` then attaches any `installation_id` it is given to the current org, whoever the authenticated GitHub user is. The guard against linking someone else's installation therefore depends on webhook timing. Consider verifying access with the user token you already have, e.g. `GET /user/installations`, and checking that `installation_id` is in the list. That works whether or not the row exists.

findings.title: Authorize URL is built by string formatting with no encoding
findings.body: `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/` (and possibly a query on some deployments), and it goes into the query string unencoded. GitHub tolerates this today, as the test shows, but `urlencode({...})` is the safe way to build the query and is what `OAuth2LoginView` does.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body: The test now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which doesn't match the pipeline signature. It fails at the state check (integration.py:412) with "Invalid installation request." and never reaches `build_integration`. That leaves the 404 branch that raises "The GitHub installation could not be found." (integration.py:354-356) untested, while the test name still claims to cover it. Use the real state so the flow gets to the installation lookup, and keep the original assertion.

findings.title: No tests for the new OAuth failure paths or a successful sender match
findings.body: Nothing tests a token exchange that returns no `access_token`, a `/user` response without `login`, or a reinstall where the existing Integration's `sender.login` matches the authenticated user (the success case of the new check). `test_github_user_mismatch` only covers the mismatch. Adding these would have caught the KeyError and the 500 paths reported above.

contracts.action: New OAuthLoginView step added before GitHubInstallation; redirects to GitHub authorize with state=pipeline.signature and checks it on return
contracts.before_after: The generic OAuth2 views bind a random state into the pipeline and compare it on callback. The new view uses pipeline.signature, a constant md5 of the view class names.
contracts.visible_effect: The user is sent to GitHub's authorize page, then back to /extensions/github/setup/ and on to the app install page or the installation step.
contracts.failure_mode: The state is the same for every session, so a forged callback passes the check (login CSRF).

contracts.action: Exchange the code for an access token and fetch the GitHub user
contracts.before_after: Only the body parse is inside try/except; safe_urlopen and get_user_info (which calls raise_for_status) are not.
contracts.visible_effect: On success, github_authenticated_user is bound and the pipeline advances. A missing token or login renders the failure dialog.
contracts.failure_mode: A network error or an HTTP error from /user raises an unhandled exception (500) and the opener gets no postMessage.

contracts.action: Compare the authenticated GitHub login with integration.metadata['sender']['login'] when an Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration
contracts.equivalent_path: GitHubIntegrationsInstallationEndpoint in integrations/github/installation.py, which guards on 'sender' not in metadata
contracts.before_after: installation.py checks that the key exists before reading it; the new code indexes it directly.
contracts.visible_effect: On mismatch, the 'Invalid installation request.' dialog is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: An Integration created through the pipeline has no sender (build_integration only adds it from webhook state), so reinstalling after an uninstall raises KeyError. If no Integration row exists yet, the check is skipped entirely.

summary: The PR adds a GitHub OAuth step before installation and rejects reinstalls when the authenticated user isn't the original installer. Main problems: (1) the OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a constant md5 of the view class names that is identical for everyone, so it doesn't stop forged callbacks; (2) `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError for integrations created through the Sentry pipeline, which never store a sender, so reinstalling after an uninstall gives a 500; (3) errors from `safe_urlopen` and from `get_user_info` (which calls `raise_for_status`) aren't caught, so users get a 500 page instead of the error dialog; (4) the installer check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet, e.g. before the webhook arrives. `test_installation_not_found` now stops at a state mismatch and no longer tests the 404 path. The `pipeline_advancer.py` change is a behaviour-preserving inline of `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR`.
